```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Clements_2026_belantamab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Clements_2026_belantamab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70337> (open access)
* Supplement (Tables S1-S4, Figures S1-S6 and the NONMEM control stream):
  Supporting Information of the same article.

Clements 2026 fits one simultaneous model to four analytes measured in
patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma who received the anti-BCMA
antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) belantamab mafodotin as monotherapy: total
belantamab mafodotin, free soluble BCMA (sBCMA), belantamab mafodotin-sBCMA
complex, and serum M-protein. It merges the earlier population PK model
(`modellib("Rathi_2021_belantamab")`) and M-protein model
(`modellib("Collins_2023_belantamab_mprotein")`) and then simplifies the
result with local and global sensitivity analyses.

# Population

The analysis dataset (Clements 2026 Table 1) holds 510 patients from four
studies: DREAMM-1 (n = 45; 0.03-3.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks), DREAMM-2 (n = 216;
2.5 or 3.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks), DREAMM-3 (n = 215; 2.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks)
and the DREAMM-5 monotherapy arm (n = 34; 2.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks). Median
(range) age was 66 (34-89) years and baseline weight 74.7 (37-142) kg; 45.9%
were female, 80.4% White, 8.0% Black and 11.4% Asian. Baseline medians were
sBCMA 72.9 ng/mL (2.08-2030), M-protein 18.0 g/L (0.7-102) and albumin
38.0 g/L. Patients needed a quantifiable baseline serum M-protein above
0.5 g/L. The dataset held 4586 total-ADC, 4624 free-sBCMA, 3422
complex-sBCMA and 3228 M-protein observations.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Clements_2026_belantamab")()$population`.

# Model structure

The published NONMEM control stream (Supporting Information) is the model that
was fitted, and the packaged model follows it line by line. With $C_T$ the
total and $C_F$ the free belantamab mafodotin concentration, $S_T$ the total
sBCMA concentration (all nM), $R$ the sBCMA reservoir and $M$ the serum
M-protein (g/L):

* Quasi-equilibrium binding:
  $C_F = \tfrac12\left[(C_T - S_T - K_D) + \sqrt{(C_T - S_T - K_D)^2 + 4 K_D C_T}\right]$,
  complex $= S_T C_F / (K_D + C_F)$.
* Total drug: elimination $K_{EL} C_F V_C + K_{INT} \cdot \text{complex} \cdot V_C$
  with $K_{INT} = K_{EL} = CL/V_C$, so total-drug clearance is linear; total
  drug (free + bound) distributes to the peripheral compartment.
* $dS_T/dt = K_{DIFF} R - (K_{INT} - K_{DEG}) \cdot \text{complex} - K_{DEG} S_T$.
* $dM/dt = K_{GR} (1 - M/150) M - K_{DEATH} C_F M$.
* $dR/dt = K_{SYN} M / M_{BL} - K_{DIFF} R$, with $K_{SYN} = K_{DEG} \cdot \text{sBCMA}_{BL} / 6$.
* $S_T(0) = R(0) = \text{sBCMA}_{BL}/6$ (nM) and $M(0) = M_{BL}$.

The dose is supplied in mg. The ADC state is held in mg and converted to nM
with the control-stream molecular weight of 152.1 kDa; sBCMA is converted from
ng/mL with 6 kDa. Free and complexed sBCMA observations carry the paper's
assay-dilution correction (dilution factor 20 for free, 10 for complexed
sBCMA), and every output has the control-stream lower floor applied before the
log transform.

| Model name | Paper name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `central`, `peripheral1` | ADCc, ADCp | Total belantamab mafodotin (mg) |
| `total_target` | SBCMAt | Total sBCMA in the central compartment (nM) |
| `precursor1` | SBCMAr | sBCMA reservoir (nM) |
| `mprotein` | MPROT | Serum M-protein (g/L) |
| `kkill` | KDEATH | M-protein kill rate per unit free drug |
| `p` | KGR | M-protein growth rate |
| `kpout` | KDIFF | Diffusion out of the sBCMA reservoir |
| `Cc` | CP1C | Total belantamab mafodotin (nM) |
| `sbcma_free`, `sbcma_complex` | CP3FC, CP3CC | Free and complexed sBCMA as measured (nM) |
| `mprotein_obs` | CPM | M-protein as measured (g/L) |

# Structural checks

The checks below use the typical male reference patient (74.65 kg, albumin
38 g/L, sBCMA 72.85 ng/mL, M-protein 18 g/L, no extramedullary disease) and
compare the solve with quantities that follow exactly from the equations.

```{r typical-solve}
mod <- readModelDb("Clements_2026_belantamab")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ref_cov <- data.frame(WT = 74.65, ALB = 38, SBCMA = 72.85, SEXF = 0, DIS_EMD = 0, MCPROT = 18)
mw_adc <- 152.1
inf_dur <- 0.5 / 24

make_events <- function(dose, times, ii = 0, addl = 0, n = 1, cov = ref_cov) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, dur = inf_dur, cmt = "central", ii = ii, addl = addl) |>
    rxode2::et(times) |>
    rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n)) |>
    as.data.frame()
  # A zero dose gets no dose record: rxode2 5.1.8.9000 fails the subject on a
  # zero-amount infusion with a duration.
  if (dose == 0) ev <- ev[ev$evid == 0, ]
  # Multi-endpoint model: observation rows carry a dvid instead of a state name.
  ev$cmt[ev$evid == 0] <- NA_character_
  ev$dvid <- 1L
  cov$id <- seq_len(nrow(cov))
  dplyr::left_join(ev, cov, by = "id")
}

typ_times <- sort(unique(c(0, inf_dur, seq(0.05, 1, by = 0.05), seq(1, 150, by = 0.5))))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, make_events(200, typ_times),
  returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10
)
```

**Quasi-equilibrium binding.** Free drug, free sBCMA and complex must satisfy
$K_D = C_F \cdot S_F / \text{complex}$ and the mass balances
$S_F + \text{complex} = S_T$ at every time point. These are identities of the
same solve, so the tolerance is numerical.

```{r check-binding}
chk_bind <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  mutate(
    kd_implied = cf_obs * sbcma_free_true / sbcma_cplx_true,
    mass_err = (sbcma_free_true + sbcma_cplx_true) / total_target - 1
  )
stopifnot(
  max(abs(chk_bind$kd_implied / 1.11 - 1)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(chk_bind$mass_err)) < 1e-10
)
```

**Total drug is linear.** Because $K_{INT} = K_{EL}$, total belantamab
mafodotin follows an ordinary linear two-compartment model whatever the sBCMA
level. The solve is compared with the closed-form two-compartment infusion
solution.

```{r check-linear}
twocmt_infusion <- function(t, dose, tinf, cl, v1, q, v2) {
  k10 <- cl / v1; k12 <- q / v1; k21 <- q / v2
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  l1 <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  l2 <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  a1 <- (l1 - k21) / (l1 - l2) / v1
  a2 <- (k21 - l2) / (l1 - l2) / v1
  rate <- dose / tinf
  term <- function(a, l) {
    ifelse(
      t <= tinf,
      rate * a / l * (1 - exp(-l * t)),
      rate * a / l * (1 - exp(-l * tinf)) * exp(-l * (t - tinf))
    )
  }
  term(a1, l1) + term(a2, l2)
}
chk_lin <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  mutate(closed = twocmt_infusion(time, 200, inf_dur, 0.7, 4.81, 0.771, 12.7) * 1000 / mw_adc)
stopifnot(max(abs(chk_lin$ctot / chk_lin$closed - 1)) < 1e-5)
```

**Drug-free sBCMA transient.** The reservoir starts at the baseline sBCMA
concentration rather than at its drug-free steady state
$K_{SYN}/K_{DIFF} = (K_{DEG}/K_{DIFF}) \cdot \text{sBCMA}_{BL}$ (Methods,
"Model Finalization"; control stream `A_0(5)`). Without drug the reservoir
therefore empties into the central pool during the first days, and total
sBCMA rises before returning to baseline. With M-protein held at baseline the
excess is
$x(t) = \frac{K_{DIFF} y_0}{K_{DEG} - K_{DIFF}} (e^{-K_{DIFF} t} - e^{-K_{DEG} t})$
with $y_0 = S_0 (1 - K_{DEG}/K_{DIFF})$. M-protein grows by under 2% over the
first five days, so the comparison uses a 2% tolerance.

```{r check-transient}
ev_nodrug <- make_events(0, seq(0, 5, by = 0.1))
sim_nodrug <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_nodrug, returnType = "data.frame")
s0 <- 72.85 / 6
y0 <- s0 * (1 - 0.671 / 4.45)
chk_tr <- sim_nodrug |>
  mutate(analytic = s0 + 4.45 * y0 / (0.671 - 4.45) * (exp(-4.45 * time) - exp(-0.671 * time)))
stopifnot(max(abs(chk_tr$total_target / chk_tr$analytic - 1)) < 0.02)
max(chk_tr$total_target) / s0
```

Free sBCMA in a drug-free patient therefore peaks at about
`r round(max(chk_tr$total_target) / s0, 2)` times its baseline value
`r round(chk_tr$time[which.max(chk_tr$total_target)], 1)` days after time zero.
This is a property of the published model, not a physiological claim, and in
practice the first dose is given at time zero.

# Virtual cohort

Clements 2026 simulated from a covariate population built by multivariate
imputation from the analysis dataset, which is not published. The cohort below
is drawn independently for each covariate to match the Table 1 medians and
ranges: log-normal weight, sBCMA and M-protein, normal albumin, 45.9% female
and 10% with extramedullary disease (the prevalence is not reported).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(74.7), 0.2), 37), 142),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 38, 5), 19), 52.3),
  SBCMA = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(72.9), 1.1), 2.08), 2030),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.459),
  DIS_EMD = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.10),
  MCPROT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(18), 0.8), 0.7), 102)
)
summary(cohort)
```

# Figure 5: dose and schedule simulations

Figure 5 of Clements 2026 shows median profiles over 28 days for 30, 100, 200
and 300 mg every 2 weeks (Q2W) or every 4 weeks (Q4W). Each regimen is solved
for the same 200 patients with the same random-effect draws (the seed is reset
before every solve), so differences between regimens are due to dose alone.

```{r fig5-sim}
fig5_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 28, by = 0.25), 1 / 24, 14 + 1 / 24)))
regimens <- expand.grid(dose = c(30, 100, 200, 300), freq = c("Q2W", "Q4W"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fig5 <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  ev <- make_events(r$dose, fig5_times, ii = if (r$freq == "Q2W") 14 else 0,
                    addl = if (r$freq == "Q2W") 1 else 0, n = n_sub, cov = cohort)
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$dose <- r$dose
  s$freq <- r$freq
  s
}) |> bind_rows()

fig5_med <- fig5 |>
  mutate(
    total_ngml = ctot * mw_adc,
    free_adc_nM = cfree,
    pct_unbound = 100 * cfree / pmax(ctot, 1e-12),
    free_sbcma_ngml = sbcma_free_true * 6,
    cplx_sbcma_ngml = sbcma_cplx_true * 6,
    mprot_ratio = mprotein / MCPROT
  ) |>
  group_by(dose, freq, time) |>
  summarise(across(c(total_ngml, free_adc_nM, pct_unbound, free_sbcma_ngml, cplx_sbcma_ngml, mprotein, mprot_ratio), median),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
fig5_med |>
  select(dose, freq, time,
         `Total ADC (ng/mL)` = total_ngml, `Free ADC (nM)` = free_adc_nM,
         `Percent unbound ADC (%)` = pct_unbound, `Free sBCMA (ng/mL)` = free_sbcma_ngml,
         `Complexed sBCMA (ng/mL)` = cplx_sbcma_ngml, `M-protein (g/L)` = mprotein) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(dose, freq, time)) |>
  filter(value > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = factor(dose), linetype = freq)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Median", colour = "Dose (mg)", linetype = "Schedule",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Clements 2026.") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig5-table}
fig5_med |>
  filter(time %in% c(1, 7, 14, 28)) |>
  select(dose, freq, time, total_ngml, pct_unbound, free_sbcma_ngml, cplx_sbcma_ngml, mprot_ratio) |>
  mutate(across(c(total_ngml, pct_unbound, free_sbcma_ngml, cplx_sbcma_ngml), ~ signif(.x, 3)),
         mprot_ratio = round(mprot_ratio, 3)) |>
  rename(`Dose (mg)` = dose, Schedule = freq, `Day` = time,
         `Total ADC (ng/mL)` = total_ngml, `Unbound (%)` = pct_unbound,
         `Free sBCMA (ng/mL)` = free_sbcma_ngml, `Complexed sBCMA (ng/mL)` = cplx_sbcma_ngml,
         `M-protein / baseline` = mprot_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The simulations reproduce the dose ordering the paper reports: higher doses
give lower free sBCMA, higher complexed sBCMA and lower M-protein after the
first dose, and Q2W dosing lowers M-protein further than Q4W by day 28. The
checks below hold patient by patient because each regimen reuses the same
patients and random effects.

```{r fig5-checks}
day1 <- fig5_med |> filter(freq == "Q2W", time == 1) |> arrange(dose)
day28_q2w <- fig5_med |> filter(freq == "Q2W", time == 28) |> arrange(dose)
day28 <- fig5_med |> filter(time == 28) |>
  select(dose, freq, mprot_ratio) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = freq, values_from = mprot_ratio)
# Complexed sBCMA saturates above 100 mg (200 and 300 mg differ by under 1%),
# so only the 30 mg versus 300 mg contrast is asserted for it.
stopifnot(
  all(diff(day1$free_sbcma_ngml) < 0),
  day1$cplx_sbcma_ngml[day1$dose == 300] > 1.2 * day1$cplx_sbcma_ngml[day1$dose == 30],
  all(diff(day28_q2w$mprot_ratio) < 0),
  all(day28$Q2W <= day28$Q4W)
)
```

The absolute levels in Figure 5 do not match the model's parameters, and the
differences cannot be removed without changing parameter values, which this
package does not do. Read from the published panels by eye: the free sBCMA
baseline is about 25 ng/mL, whereas the Table 1 median sBCMA, which sets the
model's baseline, is 72.9 ng/mL; the "Free ADC (ng/mL)" panel peaks near
200 at 200 mg, which matches free drug in nM rather than ng/mL; and median
M-protein falls by about 40% within a week at 200 mg, against
`r round(100 * (1 - fig5_med$mprot_ratio[fig5_med$dose == 200 & fig5_med$freq == "Q2W" & fig5_med$time == 7]))`%
here.
The free-ADC panel shows that at least one Figure 5 axis label is wrong. The
packaged parameters are the Table 2 estimates, the structure follows the
published control stream line by line, and the simulations below are
broadly consistent with the paper's prediction-corrected VPC (Figure 3). The
remaining differences are therefore taken to come from the Figure 5
simulation set-up, which the paper does not describe in enough detail to
reproduce.

# Figure 3: VPC-style simulation at the approved regimen

Figure 3 of Clements 2026 is a prediction-corrected VPC across all four
studies, whose patients mostly received 2.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks. The cohort
below receives 2.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks for about 10 months.

```{r fig3-sim}
fig3_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 1 / 24, seq(1, 300, by = 1))))
ev3 <- make_events(1, fig3_times, ii = 21, addl = 14, n = n_sub, cov = cohort)
ev3$amt[ev3$evid == 1] <- 2.5 * ev3$WT[ev3$evid == 1]
ev3$treatment <- "2.5 mg/kg Q3W"
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
fig3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev3, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "treatment")
if (!"id" %in% names(fig3)) fig3$id <- 1L

fig3_pct <- fig3 |>
  select(id, time, `Total ADC (nM)` = Cc, `Free sBCMA (nM)` = sbcma_free,
         `Complexed sBCMA (nM)` = sbcma_complex, `M-protein (g/L)` = mprotein_obs) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, time)) |>
  group_by(name, time) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(value, 0.05), p50 = median(value), p95 = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(fig3_pct, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Median and 90% interval (no residual error)",
       caption = "Compare with Figure 3 of Clements 2026 (prediction-corrected VPC).") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig3-table}
fig3_tab <- fig3_pct |>
  filter(time %in% c(1 / 24, 20, 100, 200, 300))
fig3_tab |>
  mutate(time = round(time, 2), across(c(p05, p50, p95), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  rename(Analyte = name, Day = time, `5th pct` = p05, Median = p50, `95th pct` = p95) |>
  knitr::kable()
med_at <- function(analyte, day) {
  signif(fig3_tab$p50[fig3_tab$name == analyte & abs(fig3_tab$time - day) < 1e-6], 2)
}
```

The simulated median M-protein falls from
`r med_at("M-protein (g/L)", 20)` g/L at day 20 to
`r med_at("M-protein (g/L)", 100)` g/L at day 100 and
`r med_at("M-protein (g/L)", 300)` g/L at day 300. Figure 3D, read by eye,
shows medians of about 10-12 g/L at day 100 and about 5 g/L at day 300. The
paper's VPC follows each patient's actual dosing and, in its later bins, only
the patients still on study, who are enriched for responders, while this
simulation keeps every patient on uninterrupted treatment; a slower fall in
the median here is the expected direction. The median total ADC at the end of
the first infusion is `r med_at("Total ADC (nM)", 1 / 24)` nM, against
roughly 10^2.5 nM for the first peak in Figure 3C. Troughs are not compared:
in a prediction-corrected VPC the trough bins mix samples taken at different
times after the dose. The comparison is visual.

# Figure 4: M-protein reduction at nadir

Figure 4 compares the proportions of patients reaching each maximum M-protein
reduction with the model predictions for each study. Its predictions use each
study's actual dosing and follow-up, which are not published; the table below
uses six months (nine cycles) of 2.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks.

```{r fig4}
nadir <- fig3 |>
  filter(time <= 182) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(red = 1 - min(mprotein) / first(MCPROT)) |>
  mutate(category = cut(red, c(-Inf, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, Inf), right = FALSE,
                        labels = c(">=0-<25% (or increase)", ">=25-<50%", ">=50-<90%", ">=90%")))
nadir_tab <- as.data.frame(table(nadir$category))
names(nadir_tab) <- c("category", "n")
nadir_tab |>
  mutate(
    simulated = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
    paper_dreamm2 = c(44, 24, 23, 9),
    paper_dreamm3 = c(41, 24, 23, 12)
  ) |>
  select(-n) |>
  rename(`Maximum decrease` = category, `Simulated (%)` = simulated,
         `DREAMM-2 model median (%)` = paper_dreamm2, `DREAMM-3 model median (%)` = paper_dreamm3) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The paper's predicted percentages were read from Figure 4 by eye. Like the
paper, the simulation puts the largest share of patients below a 25%
reduction, but it predicts more patients with a reduction of 90% or more and
fewer between 25% and 50% than the paper's per-study predictions. The paper's
predictions use the doses each patient actually received; dose delays and
reductions were frequent with belantamab mafodotin, and patients stopped
treatment at progression, whereas this simulation gives every patient nine
uninterrupted full doses. With the large between-subject variability on the
M-protein growth rate (CV 314%) and kill rate (CV 134%), uninterrupted dosing
lets the most sensitive patients reach very deep reductions. The comparison is
indicative only.

# PKNCA: total belantamab mafodotin

The paper reports no NCA. Two PKNCA analyses check the total-drug PK.

**First-dose exposure at 2.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks** in the virtual cohort:

```{r pknca-cohort}
conc_first <- fig3 |>
  filter(time <= 21) |>
  transmute(id, time, Cc = ctot, treatment) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_first <- ev3 |>
  filter(evid == 1, time == 0) |>
  transmute(id, time, amt, treatment = "2.5 mg/kg Q3W")
o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc_first, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(dose_first, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
o_data <- PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose,
                    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 21, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE))
o_nca <- pk.nca(o_data)
summary(o_nca)
```

**Single doses in the typical patient.** Total drug is linear, so
$AUC_{0-\infty}$ must equal dose / CL (converted to nM*day) at every dose,
and the terminal half-life must equal $\ln 2 / \lambda_2$ of the
two-compartment model.

```{r pknca-typical}
doses_sd <- c(30, 100, 200, 300)
sd_times <- sort(unique(c(0, inf_dur, seq(0.25, 2, by = 0.25), seq(3, 400, by = 1))))
sim_sd <- lapply(doses_sd, function(d) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, make_events(d, sd_times), returnType = "data.frame",
                       atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10)
  if (!"id" %in% names(s)) s$id <- 1L
  s$dose <- d
  s
}) |> bind_rows()

conc_sd <- sim_sd |>
  transmute(id = 1L, time, Cc = ctot, treatment = paste(dose, "mg")) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_sd <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = doses_sd, treatment = paste(doses_sd, "mg"))
sd_nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(conc_sd, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCAdose(dose_sd, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
sd_res <- as.data.frame(sd_nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(dose = as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", treatment)),
         auc_expected = dose / 0.7 * 1000 / mw_adc)

k10 <- 0.7 / 4.81; k12 <- 0.771 / 4.81; k21 <- 0.771 / 12.7
s_sum <- k10 + k12 + k21
lambda2 <- (s_sum - sqrt(s_sum^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
sd_res |>
  mutate(t_half_expected = log(2) / lambda2) |>
  select(Dose = treatment, `Cmax (nM)` = cmax, `AUC0-inf (nM*day)` = aucinf.obs,
         `Dose/CL (nM*day)` = auc_expected, `t1/2 (day)` = half.life,
         `ln2/lambda2 (day)` = t_half_expected) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sd_res$aucinf.obs / sd_res$auc_expected - 1)) < 0.01,
  max(abs(sd_res$half.life / (log(2) / lambda2) - 1)) < 0.01
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose units.** The control stream defines `MWADC = 152.1` and mixes the
  central drug concentration with sBCMA (nM) and KD (nM) in one expression,
  and Figure 3C reports total ADC in nM, so the fitted dataset carried the
  dose in nmol. The packaged model takes the dose in mg and converts with the
  same molecular weight.
* **Reservoir initial condition.** The reservoir starts at baseline sBCMA, as
  the Methods and the control stream state, rather than at its steady state;
  see the drug-free transient check above.
* **Fixed random effects.** The control stream carries random effects on QA,
  KDEG, KD and KDIFF with variances fixed to 0.0225. Table 2 lists only the
  estimated variances; the fixed ones are included here as `fixed(0.0225)`.
  Use `rxode2::zeroRe()` for typical-value simulation.
* **Control-stream values.** The `$THETA` values in the published control
  stream are initial estimates (for example VP 29.1 L, the value before the
  final model change); every packaged estimate comes from Table 2. The
  beta-2-microglobulin effect on CL is fixed to zero in the control stream and
  is left out.
* **KD units.** Table 2 gives KD in "nM/L" and the control-stream comment says
  "uM"; nM is the unit consistent with the dataset and the sBCMA conversion.
* **Text versus Table 2.** The Results text gives RSEs of 46.6% (sBCMA on
  CLADC) and 37.8% (sex on CLADC) and BSV RSEs of at least 55.9%, which differ
  from Table 2 (13.5%, 32.1%, 38.1% and 7.82%). Only the point estimates are
  used here, and those are the Table 2 values.
* **Figure 5.** The published medians are not reproduced quantitatively (see
  the Figure 5 section); the dose ordering is.
* **Figures 3 and 4.** These depend on each patient's actual dosing and
  follow-up, which are not published. The simulations here use uninterrupted
  2.5 mg/kg every 3 weeks, so the comparisons are visual only.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariates are sampled independently from distributions
  matched to the Table 1 medians and ranges; the prevalence of extramedullary
  disease (10%) is assumed.
* **Erratum search.** No erratum or correction was found for Clements 2026 as
  of 2026-11-18.
